tasks.title: Make a long conversation fall over
tasks.description:
In `src/reproduce.ts`, implement `reproduceOverflow()`.

Start one `ChatSession` and send it the questions from `src/questions.ts`, one at a time, until `send` throws. Return:

- `turns`: which send failed, counting from 1
- `error`: the message of the error it threw

The check runs your function against the original `chat.ts`.
nextSteps: Run `node src/demo.ts` and watch the number of messages kept grow.
Loop over `questions` and await `send` for each one.
Catch the first error and return its turn number and message.
hints: The demo already shows the failure. Your job is to capture it as data.
Use `questions.entries()` or a counter so you know which send you are on when it throws.
Put the `try`/`catch` inside the loop and `return { turns: i + 1, error: (err as Error).message }` from the catch.

tasks.title: Keep the conversation inside the window
tasks.description:
Fix `ChatSession` in `src/chat.ts` so a conversation can go on as long as the customer likes.

Team policy:

- The system prompt always stays as `history[0]`.
- After it, keep at most `MAX_RECENT_MESSAGES` messages: the most recent ones.
- The request sent to the model follows the same rule.
- Short conversations are not trimmed at all.

Keep the class name, the `history` property and the `send` signature.
nextSteps: Count how many messages `send` passes to the model on each turn.
Decide where in `send` the history should be trimmed.
Keep the system prompt separate from the messages you trim.
Run `node src/demo.ts` and check the count stays flat.
hints: The model refuses once the whole history no longer fits its context window. Nothing ever removes old messages.
Split the history into the first message and the rest. Only the rest gets cut down.
`rest.slice(-MAX_RECENT_MESSAGES)` keeps the newest messages. Rebuild the history from the system prompt plus that, before the request and after the reply.

tasks.title: Write the test that would have caught it
tasks.description:
Write vitest tests in `src/chat.test.ts` that check:

- a session can answer all 30 questions in `questions.ts` without an error
- after a long conversation Kes still follows the system prompt: replies start with `Kes here.` and `history[0]` is still the system prompt

The check runs your test file beside the original `chat.ts` (it must fail), beside a correct fix (it must pass) and beside a fix that simply drops the oldest messages (it must fail).
nextSteps: Write a test that sends every question.
Write a test that inspects the last reply and `history[0]` afterwards.
Run `npx vitest run src/chat.test.ts` against your fixed code.
hints: Use a fresh `ChatSession` in each test so they do not depend on each other.
The local model only introduces itself as Kes when the first message it receives is the system prompt.
Dropping the oldest messages also drops the system prompt. Assert on the last reply's opening words and on `history[0]`.
